answer: A yarrow bridge spans a wide gorge, and every new identity must spin one more plume of yarrow fibre into rope before it may cross. The first fake spins 1 arm-length, the second 3, the third 9, so the tenth fake alone spins 19,683 lengths and twenty fakes together spin 1,743,392,200. The rope grows threefold each time because every new span must be braided from the rope that came before it. Bulk farming fails because a single spindle spins one thread at a time and each new length is wound onto the last, like one weaver finishing one rope before the next can begin. Bought rope never holds.
